title: Constant Areal Rate in Uniform Circular Motion
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A point moves around a circle of radius r with constant period T, completing one revolution in time T. Modeling the swept sector area as a function of time, show that equal time intervals sweep equal areas, and determine the areal rate.

steps.title: Write the Angular Position Law
steps.explanation: Uniform motion means the angle advances linearly: over time t the fraction t/T of a full turn 2*pi has been completed.
steps.why: Constant period and no speed variation force a linear angle law with angular speed omega = 2*pi/T.

steps.title: Convert Angle to Swept Sector Area
steps.explanation: The area of a circular sector with radian angle theta is (1/2) r^2 theta; substituting the linear angle law makes A a linear function of time.
steps.why: Sector area is proportional to its central angle, and proportionality composed with linearity in t stays linear in t.

steps.title: Read Off the Constant Areal Rate
steps.explanation: Because A(t) is a linear function, the area swept over any interval of length delta-t equals (pi r^2/T) times delta-t, independent of where the interval starts.
steps.why: Linearity of A guarantees equal inputs produce equal outputs: this is the exact statement of 'equal areas in equal times'.

steps.title: Sanity-Check Against the Whole Disk
steps.explanation: One full period must sweep the entire disk of area pi*r^2, and the formula reproduces this total exactly.
steps.why: A correct areal-rate law must integrate over a period to the full circle area; the check confirms no missing factor.
